title: Remember the Rutherglen 'poltergeist' that left police calling in a priest?
excerpt: Police Scotland officers saw clothes fly and lights move during a baffling 2016 disturbance at a Rutherglen home, prompting a Catholic house blessing.
content:
Police officers were left baffled after witnessing clothes fly across a room during a call-out in South Lanarkshire.

The bizarre incident unfolded when mother Catherine Shreenan, who was 51 at the time, contacted Police Scotland to report an unexplained disturbance at her home on Stonelaw Road in Rutherglen in August 2016.

Officers with decades of experience on the force arrived at the property expecting a routine call, but encountered scenes they could not explain.

Police witnessed clothes fly across the room, light shades turn upside down, and the family chihuahua dog appear on top of a seven-foot garden hedge.

The bewildered officers subsequently called in the Catholic Church to bless the house after finding no logical explanation for the events.

A police source said at the time that officers looked into the history of the property to establish whether there was any rational explanation for the strange occurrences.

Ms Shreenan, who had been living at the property with her son, fled to her parents' home just miles away in South Lanarkshire after the incident.

She told the Glasgow Times that worldwide attention over her haunted home had placed her family under severe stress.

The incident triggered widespread public fascination and prompted paranormal investigator Ally Key, from Dundee, and his wife Sadie to appeal publicly to help the family.

Mr Key said: "A professional, experienced person needs to help this family. The disturbance description doesn't sound like a poltergeist, it sounds like an intelligent entity."

He added: "Spirits can appear and leave at any time. It can be attached to a building or a person, or be an entity arriving because of a dramatic change in the atmosphere or structure of a home - possibly the spirit's old home.

"We would need to conduct a full investigation to determine if there is a logical explanation or if a spirit is inhabiting the property."

The psychic medium, who claimed to communicate with the dead alongside his spirit guide Father Joseph, offered to spend two nights at the Stonelaw Road flat to investigate away from the media spotlight.

Mr Key said: "I've never failed a case; we've always found an answer, paranormal or not. We want to help without a media circus or mass hysteria."

The bizarre disturbance remains one of the most unusual incidents ever documented in Police Scotland's modern call logs.
